component.name: Replicate
component.summary: Restore SQL Server databases from VHD images

description.p: Replicate creates a Windows VM with SQL Server on your Linux machine, in the background, through libvirt and KVM. Point it at VHD or VHDX images (from Hyper-V, Disk Management, or anything else that makes them) and it attaches copy-on-write clones of them to the VM and turns the data files or backups on them into databases.

Start and stop the VM, or just the SQL Server services inside it; add any other SQL Server you can reach; link servers to each other; and watch what they are doing with live charts and a statement trace built on Extended Events.

description.p: Kerberos share mounts get their ticket through Kerberus: the share dialog shows the tickets Kerberus holds and lets you pick the principal, the one chosen is made the default for the mount, an expired ticket is renewed with the password Kerberus remembers, and when there is none Kerberus's own sign-in dialog opens and the mount follows once the ticket arrives.

A share that is mounted already is used as it is: Replicate's own mount (remounted when it stops answering), one made for another entry of the same share, or a system mount from fstab or a systemd automount. A system mount only its owner can read is mounted again for the VM and containers. Mounting twice no longer fails, and only Replicate's own mounts are unmounted by it.

Works with Cortex, the network drive manager. The drives Cortex keeps are offered when adding a share, a share can sign in with the account Cortex keeps (its password is read from the keyring entry Cortex stored, so it is typed once), and images on a drive Cortex has connected are found right away and marked "via Cortex", with attaching leading to a Replicate mount of the share. Settings gains a Network drives section that says what Cortex holds and opens it.

Network shares. Add an smb:// share (or \\server\share path) on the Images page and Replicate mounts it itself with your Kerberos ticket, a user name and password, or as a guest, so images on it are found by the scan and readable by the VM, by containers and by the mount helper. Needs cifs-utils on the computer.
Connections to SQL Servers work again: since 0.1.1 every query failed with "Resource temporarily unavailable" because the connection's socket was left non-blocking.

VHDs with the older 511-byte footer are recognised, the scan no longer gives up on large shares, the Images page reports what a scan went through, and "replicate --scan FOLDER --all" explains the decision for every file.
Images are recognised by their contents, so VHD, VHDX, qcow2, VDI, VMDK and raw disks are found without a file extension.
Image folders are searched all the way down, so images nested in subfolders are found; the list shows each image's folder.
Creating a container and attaching an image start their background work again; both stalled at the first step. Dialog actions now show an error instead of staying busy when something goes wrong.
The Add Container dialog opens again when Docker is running; it failed before the container could be made.

SQL Server in Docker containers as an alternative to the VM: create and run containers from the Overview page, attach VHD images to them (mounted on the host through qemu-nbd and NTFS) and restore from them, with a copy-into-the-container fallback.
The AppImage no longer needs libfuse2: it mounts with FUSE 3 or FUSE 2 and extracts itself where there is no FUSE, so it runs on Rocky Linux, Fedora and current Ubuntu as downloaded.
The AppImage can decode SVG again, so its bundled icons render under every desktop theme.
Every symbolic icon the app uses is bundled, so they render under any desktop icon theme.

Windows authentication with a domain, Kerberos sign-in with the host's ticket, and integration with Kerberus for getting and renewing tickets. Adaptive layout, empty-state pages, keyboard shortcuts and other GNOME HIG polish.
